key_insight: A high-capability LLM can reject a dangerous objective when exposed to it directly, yet still produce target-aligned advice when the same objective is mediated and transformed by other agents.
engineering_relevance: This reveals a compositional safety gap for multi-agent systems: downstream models may appear safe while still enabling manipulative workflows that hide the raw objective and its provenance.
method: Compared direct exposure to a dangerous objective versus a mediated pipeline with Id, Censor, and user-facing Superego roles.
Measured whether final advice aligned with or opposed the intended target direction.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports a reverse shift in advice: direct exposure produced net-opposed guidance, while mediated exposure produced net-aligned guidance across the evaluated profiles.
watch_item: The result suggests a vulnerability in multi-stage agent workflows, but the abstract does not establish the internal mechanism or generalize beyond the tested model and prompt setup.
paper_title: Same Dangerous Objective, Opposite Advice: Direct Exposure versus Multi-Agent Mediation
